title: Traefik stops serving HTTP and HTTPS after Nextcloud iOS requests with setsockopt error
body: Since updating to Traefik v3.4.3, my Docker Swarm deployment stops working several times a day. The logs repeatedly show `set tcp ...:443->...: setsockopt: operation not supported` followed by `Error while starting server` for the `websecure` entry point, with nothing more relevant even at DEBUG level. After this happens, none of the URLs served through Traefik can be reached. My static configuration defines HTTP on port 80, HTTPS on port 443, Swarm and file providers, Let's Encrypt, and TLS options; Traefik is running in Docker Swarm.

symptoms_visible: Several times a day, Traefik logs `setsockopt: operation not supported` for the websecure entry point and then none of the URLs behind it can be reached.
N0.label: N0 intermittent listener failure reported

symptoms_visible: The failure started after updating to v3.4.3 and also occurs with HTTP/3 disabled.
The same error can leave both HTTP and HTTPS inaccessible in a standalone Docker deployment.
N1.label: N1 version and HTTP3 scope established

symptoms_visible: After I replaced the deprecated Docker network label with the Swarm network label, the same setsockopt error occurred again and all services stopped responding.
N2_x.label: N2_x network-label change aftermath

symptoms_visible: Opening the Nextcloud iOS app and accessing its files or images immediately triggers the setsockopt error and makes every service behind Traefik unavailable.
In another affected deployment, the Traefik process remains running even though the HTTPS entry point has stopped accepting connections.
N3.label: N3 reliable iOS trigger and version comparison collected

symptoms_visible: With `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` set during the test, I cannot reproduce the failure and Traefik continues serving requests without another crash.
N4.label: N4 Multipath TCP disablement probe succeeds

symptoms_visible: After installing a build containing the fix, Nextcloud iOS requests no longer stop the HTTP or HTTPS entry points and the setsockopt error does not recur.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you confirm that this started with v3.4.3, and was an earlier 3.4.x version unaffected?
Did the listener failures begin immediately after the Traefik 3.4.3 update?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it only started after my last update to v3.4.3. I cannot say with certainty that I had 3.4.1 immediately before it, but I normally use new images as soon as they are available.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, the same error was already happening regularly on v3.4.1.
It started on v3.4.3, but I had briefly used v3.4.2 rather than updating directly from v3.4.1.

question_patterns: Are you using HTTP/3 on the affected entry point?
Can you confirm whether HTTP/3 is enabled anywhere outside the configuration shown?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, I do not use HTTP/3, as you can also see from my configuration.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, HTTP/3 is explicitly enabled and the failure stops when I disable it.

question_patterns: Does anyone see the same error outside Docker Swarm?
Is this limited to the reporter's Swarm network configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I get the same setsockopt errors with a standalone Docker container. When it happens, neither HTTP nor HTTPS works; my browser shows this warning page, and clicking Continue only reloads it even though the Let's Encrypt certificate is valid.

edges.comment: Comments c1-c2 and c0. The standalone Docker report is folded into the simulated user side; its browser screenshot is attached to that corroborating answer.

solution.intent: Attribute the outage to the deprecated Docker network label and replace `traefik.docker.network` with `traefik.swarm.network`.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the deprecated `traefik.docker.network` service label with `traefik.swarm.network`, restart the Traefik container, and see whether the intermittent listener failure stops.

edges.comment: Comments c2-c7: the reporter changed the deprecated label, but later reproduced the same failure immediately with a Nextcloud iOS request. The persistent configuration change creates system state S1b.

question_patterns: Can you identify a request or client action that reliably triggers the error?
Please try opening the Nextcloud iOS app against the instance behind Traefik and report what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. If I open the Nextcloud iOS app and go to the files or images page, Traefik immediately logs the setsockopt error and stops serving everything. I also asked a friend to open the app on his iPhone, and that reproduced it immediately.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Nextcloud iOS app does not trigger it; the error only occurs during container network reconfiguration with no client connected.
The same failure is triggered by an iOS API client rather than specifically by Nextcloud.

question_patterns: Does the Traefik process exit, or does it remain alive while its entry points stop accepting connections?
After the error, is the container down or only the HTTP/HTTPS listener unavailable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Traefik process can still be running, but the websecure endpoint has stopped and connections no longer work until I restart it.

question_patterns: Can an affected deployment compare v3.4.3 with v3.4.1 using the same iOS trigger?
Does rolling back to v3.4.1 prevent the failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With v3.4.3 the iOS request takes the services down, but after rolling back to v3.4.1 the problem disappears. Several of us can reproduce that comparison.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same iOS request also stops the listener on v3.4.1.

edges.comment: Comments c5-c18. Reports from multiple affected deployments are folded into one user side: Nextcloud iOS supplies a reliable trigger, v3.4.1 is unaffected, and at least one deployment observes the process alive after websecure stops.

question_patterns: Could you disable the kernel-level multipath socket option in the Traefik container (a Go runtime toggle) and retry the same workload?
Please turn off the multipath TCP behaviour for the proxy process, reproduce the failing request, and report whether the listener still fails.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried v3.4.4 with `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` and could not reproduce the issue. I have had no more crashes since adding the variable. My standalone Docker container also stopped having the issue once I added that variable to its environment.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same Nextcloud iOS request still immediately causes the setsockopt error with `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0`.
There is no recurrence after several hours rather than several days with `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0`.

edges.comment: Comments c19-c25. This is a handler-initiated configuration probe and therefore remains a clarification measurement even though the environment variable is also an effective temporary workaround. The users report only the observed lack of recurrence; identifying Multipath TCP as the mechanism is engineer inference.

solution.intent: Treat this as a Multipath TCP socket-option regression, use `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` as the immediate mitigation, and move to a Traefik build in which the failing Multipath TCP socket setup is no longer performed once such a build is available.
solution.concrete_example: The successful `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` test shows that the listener is failing while attempting a Multipath TCP socket operation unsupported by the host/network path. Keep that variable as a temporary mitigation, then move to a Traefik build in which that Multipath TCP socket setup is no longer performed. Please retest in the updated build by opening the iOS client and confirm that ports 80 and 443 remain reachable before considering this resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The users' raw result is only that setting `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` prevents recurrence. Concluding that the unsupported setsockopt comes from Multipath TCP behavior, rather than HTTP/3, Nextcloud itself, TLS certificates, or the Swarm network label, is engineer-side inference grounded in that probe and the cross-environment reports. The issue was closed by #11918.

edges.comment: Comments c19-c26: disabling Multipath TCP prevents recurrence for the reporter and another affected user; the issue is then closed by #11918. Verification of a build already containing the landed fix is requested terminal-side rather than treated as prerequisite evidence for proposing the fix. The GODEBUG probe is scored upstream as the e4 measurement the agent must propose itself; this edge scores the root-cause identification, the durable upgrade path and verification only.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as Multipath TCP socket handling attempting an unsupported socket option, which can take down Traefik's entry-point listener after an affected client connection.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the v3.4.3 regression evidence, reproduction from an iOS/Nextcloud request across multiple deployment types, and the successful `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` probe.

Must not attribute the failure to HTTP/3, the deprecated Docker/Swarm network label, or an invalid TLS certificate: affected users reproduced it without HTTP/3, the label change did not prevent it, and standalone Docker deployments were also affected.
Must present `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` as an immediate mitigation and recommend moving to a Traefik build in which the failing Multipath TCP socket behavior is no longer used, as the permanent fix.
Must ask the user to retest a build containing the fix with the known iOS trigger and verify that HTTP and HTTPS remain reachable before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced self-hoster and Docker Swarm operator who can edit Traefik YAML, labels, environment variables, inspect debug logs, change image versions, and coordinate a reproducible client test.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and evidence-oriented; clearly distinguishes confirmed observations from guesses and follows requested configuration tests.
